long_description:
**Orlando Philosophy Field Day**
**Friday\, July 24\, 2026 \| 6:00 PM – 8:30 PM**
**Mead Botanical Garden \| Orlando\, FL**
**Free and open to the public**

Join us for **Orlando Philosophy Field Day**, an outdoor evening of big questions, fun games, and thoughtful conversation at Mead Botanical Garden.

This event is designed for anyone who enjoys thinking, discussing, questioning, or simply meeting curious people. No philosophy background is required. Whether you are brand new to philosophy or have been reading Plato, the Stoics, Nietzsche, critical theory, or modern ethics for years, this gathering is meant to be accessible, social, and engaging.
We will spend the evening exploring ideas through casual discussion, group activities, and conversation prompts. Expect a relaxed atmosphere where people can reflect, ask questions, share perspectives, and connect with others who enjoy meaningful dialogue.

**What to expect:**

* Big philosophical questions
* Fun games and activities
* Open conversations
* New perspectives
* Community and connection
* A welcoming space for beginners and experienced readers alike

This event is a collaboration between The Optimistic Nihilism Social Club, Orlando Stoics, Philosophy for Everyday Life, and Critical Theory Reading Group–Orlando.
Bring yourself, your curiosity, and a willingness to think, play, and discover.

**Philosophy is for everyone!**

long_description:
The event begins with a short introductory talk on Buddhism. This is followed by a guided Vajrayana Buddhist meditation. The meditation generally lasts \~20 minutes, and it is accessible and beneficial to people of all experience levels. You are welcome to stay afterwards to ask any questions or talk further.

We will have meditation cushions available, but you are welcome to bring your own if you like. Chairs can also be made available for those who need.

What Is Buddhist Meditation?

In Buddhism, meditation means "effortlessly remaining in what is". This state may be brought about by calming and holding the mind, when compassion and wisdom are realized, or by working with our bodies' energy channels and meditating on light forms of Buddhas.

About Us

Diamond Way Buddhist Center Chicago belongs to an international non-profit network of over 600 lay Diamond Way Buddhist centers of the Karma Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism, founded by Lama Ole Nydahl and under the spiritual guidance of H.H. the 17th Gyalwa Karmapa, Trinley Thaye Dorje.

Diamond Way Buddhism offers practical and effective methods to realize mind’s inherent richness for the benefit of all. With an accessible and modern style, it works with people’s confidence and desire, using every situation in life to develop fearlessness and joy. We always present a basic introduction for newcomers, and the meditations are guided in English.

To learn more about our center visit:
http://www.diamondway.org/chicago/

\*This event is free. Just come as you are and enjoy.

Hey night market fans!

Come soak in the glow of the string lights, the smell of sizzling street food, and the heavy bass of live beats right by the dance floor. We'll kick things off with fast, friendly conversations. The app handles all the pairings, so you always know exactly who you're talking to and can just focus on breaking the ice with folks from all different backgrounds. Once we wrap up the rounds, you'll select the people you vibed with the most, and we'll group up to dive into the night market.

By the time you hit the dance floor, you've already got a fun crew to share the street food and live beats with. We'll be splitting into groups of 4-6, giving you a ready-made squad to grab some spicy skewers or a cold drink before migrating to the music. Whether these guys become your go-to night market and dancing squad or it's just a fantastic evening out under the stars, you're going to have a blast.

The Plan:

- 6:00PM: Check-In. Follow the link to set up your quick profile on your phone.
- 6:05PM - 7:25PM: One-on-One Rounds. The app pairs you up for some fun, focused chats. Find out who shares your love for vibrant cultural festivals, pulsing Punjabi beats, and delicious global street food.
- 7:25PM+: Group Up & Explore. Reconnect with the people you clicked with, form a tight crew of 4-6, grab some food from the trucks, snag a drink from the outdoor bars, and head over to the dance floor together.

long_description:
If you have an ounce of romance in your soul, you must see these movie.

And, if don’t have an ounce, this movie will give you that ounce—and more to spare.

And, you get a visual tour of Rome like you may have never seen it before (of course the movie was made in 1953).

The movie is a romantic comedy with Audrey Hepburn and Gregory Peck and it is a favorite of critics and audiences alike: Rotten Tomatoes gives it 96% on the Tomatometer and 93% on the Popcornmeter. And it’s even better on the big screen. Here’s how the folks at the [Olympia Film Society](https://www.olympiafilmsociety.org/movie/roman-holiday) describe it:

“Overwhelmed by her suffocating schedule, touring European princess Ann (Audrey Hepburn) takes off for a night while in Rome. When a sedative she took from her doctor kicks in, however, she falls asleep on a park bench and is found by an American reporter, Joe Bradley (Gregory Peck), who takes her back to his apartment for safety. At work the next morning, Joe finds out Ann's regal identity and bets his editor he can get exclusive interview with her, but romance soon gets in the way.

"With Gregory Peck and Audrey Hepburn turning in superb performances, Roman Holiday is 118 minutes of sheer entertainment." - Milton Lubin, The Hollywood Reporter

If you need other reasons to come out and see it, it is being shown at the Capitol Theater where you can get beer with your popcorn and feel good about supporting the [Olympia Film Society](https://www.olympiafilmsociety.org/home).

long_description:
Join us every Friday for **[Lunch with the Poets](https://greenmountainwriters.com/poetry/lunch-with-poets-burlington-vermont/)**, a relaxed, weekly gathering of poets, writers, readers, and lovers of language at The Innovation Café in Burlington.

Whether you write poetry, enjoy listening to it, or simply appreciate creative conversation, you're invited to pull up a chair and join us for lunch.

Participants are welcome to share a poem of their own or one they love during our open reading session, or simply sit back, enjoy lunch, and listen. No experience is required, and new faces are always welcome.

**Event Schedule**

**11:45 AM – 12:15 PM**
Lunch & Conversation

Enjoy lunch, meet fellow writers and readers, and connect with members of Vermont's creative community.

**12:15 PM – 1:00 PM**
Open Poetry Readings

Participants are invited to share one or two poems. Readings are generally limited to 3–5 minutes each so everyone has an opportunity to participate.

**1:00 PM – 1:15 PM**
Meet the Poets & Networking

Stay a little longer to continue conversations, exchange ideas, and make new connections.

**Cost**
Free to attend. Food and beverages are available for purchase from The Innovation Café.
Your RSVP will help us to arrange a group table in advance. But feel free to invite friends. Simply bring your appetite and your love of words.
We look forward to seeing you there.

**Organizer's Note:** This is intended to be a welcoming and supportive gathering rather than a formal critique group. Original work, favorite poems by other authors, and first-time readers are all welcome.

We’ll be visiting Pop Thai, a restaurant I’ve found that has wonderful reviews. One of my absolute favorite Thai dishes is Khao Soi, a Northern Thai curry noodle soup that’s difficult to find in the U.S. Another favorite is Larb, a minced meat salad that’s a staple in Thailand.

Looking forward to seeing everyone again!

long_description:
This is unaffiliated but a free (donation-based) class that I’ve enjoyed so figured I’d post the info for anyone interested in joining in! The space is very attuned for meditation and spiritual practice. Again, I’m just a fellow student!

From their website:

Experience the Unique Power of Himalayan Yoga

As taught by the yogis from the Himalayas— Himalayan Yoga combines gentle postures, breathwork, and mindful relaxation techniques to connect body, mind, and spirit resulting in healing from within. Whether you’re new or experienced, this practice will leave you feeling relaxed, focused, and rejuvenated.

Benefits of Himalayan Yoga:

🌿 Enhanced flexibility, balance, and holistic strength
🌿 Tools/Techniques to cope with stress, anxiety and bring mental clarity
🌿 Energizing breathwork to uplift and restore overall health

💲 Pricing: Heartfelt donations ($10 suggested or pay what your heart desires and what you can…). All donations will go to support The Meditation Center.

📍 Location, parking & other essentials: The Meditation Center (TMC), 631 University Avenue NE, Minneapolis, MN 55413. Free parking is available across the street from TMC in the Church’s parking lot. Bring a water bottle. Yoga mat, pillows and blankets provided. Please arrive 5 minutes early and get comfortable in “the Hall of Tradition” on the main floor. No registration needed.

About Your Instructor:

Sunita Bhardwaj Gangopadhyay brings 18 years of affiliation in the Himalayan Yoga and meditation tradition. She has completed a 200-hour Teacher Training Program with Himalayan Yoga. Dedicated to helping students find balance and peace, Sunita focuses on making each class accessible and rewarding, regardless of experience level. Sunita has a PhD in Physics and a retired executive who worked in high tech industry for 25 years. She is currently the president of the Board at The Meditation Center. Native of India, Sunita currently lives in Eden Prairie, MN. She is married with two children.

"The Royal Game" a psychological drama based on the novella by Stefan Zweig. A notary public, accountant, and polymath for Royal Court of Vienna is captured in the 1938 invasion of Austria (Anschluss). He remembers the terrible confinement and every bit of the book he stole, giving him the ability to compete with the greatest of chess prodigy of their time.

long_description:
Join us for an uplifting evening of devotion and community at our Bhakti Kirtan, guided by the inspiring Subala Das! Immerse yourself in the soulful vibrations of mantra chanting, led by Subal and passionate kirtaniyas who bring the sacred sounds to life. Kirtan is a beautiful practice of call-and-response singing that opens the heart, uplifts the spirit, and connects us with the divine through the practice of bhakti.

Bhakti, a Sanskrit word meaning “devotion” or “love,” is the spiritual path of connecting with the divine through heartfelt surrender and loving service. It emphasizes cultivating a deep, personal relationship with the divine, often expressed through music, prayer, and acts of kindness. Bhakti transcends religious boundaries, welcoming everyone into its embrace of universal love.

This event is open to everyone, whether you’re new to kirtan or a seasoned practitioner. Come as you are and leave feeling nourished—body, mind, and soul. Bring your friends and family, and experience the joy of chanting and sharing a meal together in a warm and welcoming atmosphere!

*Time:* 6-8pm *Cost:* Donation

From Kalpana: "Last year I spent a year traveling across South and Southeast Asia. I began by researc
long_description:
We are honored to be joined by Kalpana Jain, Director of the Global Religion Journalism Initiative at *[The Conversation](https://theconversation.com/us)*, and publisher of a [Substack](https://kalpanajain1.substack.com) on her recent explorations in South and Southeast Asia, to discuss her Substack writings over brunch at Masala Buffet in Teele Sq. Bring your thoughts, questions, and feedback!

From Kalpana: "Last year I spent a year traveling across South and Southeast Asia. I began by researching how misinformation is reshaping our world, but along the way I found myself drawn to a deeper set of questions: What brings people together across faiths, cultures, and differences?
That journey took me to sacred sites across several religious traditions and countries. I found stories where I encountered unexpected connections across religious and cultural boundaries.

I'm now exploring these themes through a Substack and podcast. I'd love your thoughts on how to sharpen the focus, what questions I may be missing, and how to grow the project."

Kalpana suggests reading the following posts from her Substack, so we can discuss them together: ["A temple that challenges assumptions about power, generation, and religious divides](https://kalpanajain1.substack.com/p/an-indian-temple-that-challenges);" ["What oral cultures teach us about memory, healing -- and what we lose without them;"](https://kalpanajain1.substack.com/p/what-oral-cultures-could-tell-us) ["What a journey to Borobudur -- an awe-inspiring Buddhist monument -- helped me see;"](https://kalpanajain1.substack.com/p/what-a-journey-to-borobudur-an-awe) and "[Journaling during Ramadan - notes from Malaysia's coastal state of Terengganu](https://kalpanajain1.substack.com/p/journaling-during-ramadan-notes-from)." If you'd like, feel free to peruse Kalpana's other posts, and bring thoughts on them as well.

This Meetup will be conducted in Hindi, Urdu, Urdu-Hindi, Hinglish, and Urdlish. If you can have a basic discussio

long_description:
Join us on July 25 at Sarva in Back Bay as we discuss *The Loneliness of Sonia & Sunny* by Kiran Desai.

Nearly twenty years after winning the Booker Prize for *The Inheritance of Loss*, Kiran Desai returns with an ambitious novel that spans continents, generations, and cultures. At its heart is the story of Sonia and Sunny, two young Indians whose lives intersect between India and the United States as they search for love, purpose, and a sense of belonging in an increasingly globalized world. What begins as a chance encounter unfolds into a sweeping exploration of family, identity, migration, class, and the ties that connect us across time and distance.
Desai's novel is both an intimate love story and an expansive family saga, filled with vivid characters, sharp observations, and reflections on what it means to build a life between cultures. Through Sonia and Sunny's journeys, the novel examines loneliness not simply as isolation, but as a universal human experience shaped by history, family expectations, and the search for connection.

As always, our discussion will be relaxed, welcoming, and accompanied by excellent food. Whether you read every page, are still making your way through this doorstopper of a novel, or are simply curious about contemporary South Asian literature, we'd love to have you join us.
📖 Book: *The Loneliness of Sonia & Sunny* by Kiran Desai
📍 Location: Sarva, Back Bay
📅 Date: July 25
Come for the fiction, stay for the food and conversation.

long_description:
Ongoing training and study of the "Arte e Scientia d'Armizare" ("Art & Science of Armed Fighting") of Italian medieval fight-master Fiore dei Liberi. Yes, the medieval Europeans had their own martial art systems!

ARTE E SCIENTIA D'ARMIZARE

Using medieval manuscripts we are studying and practicing what European professional soldiers (mercenaries) and nobles learned about mortal combat 600 years ago in northern Italy, from fightmaster Fiore dei Liberi. The Arte e Scientia d'Armizare, which survives today in the form of several manuscripts in museums, includes hand to hand combat/grappling, dagger fighting, longsword fighting and fighting with a seven foot spear.

Your "Istruttore" (Instructor) in Fiore's Arte e Scientia d'Armizare is Colin Hatcher, a martial artist of over 40 years, beginning in 1977, with over 30 years as an instructor. In addition to a long history with the Eastern martial arts Colin has also been studying and teaching the Historical European Martial Arts (known as "HEMA") for over 20 years.

This meet-up is run by historical European martial arts (HEMA) school "Accademia del Leone" ("The Academy of the Lion"), founded in 2014.

No prior knowledge or skill is required. You will find us a welcoming group and safety is a priority. Please wear comfortable clothing and don't forget to bring water to keep hydrated.

long_description:
**Women's Circle on the Lake**

Gather in the company of other women in a mindfulness circle on Lake Michigan. Get in touch with your intuition and power during a guided meditation, breathwork, gentle stretching, and yoga. Leave firmly rooted, inspired, and grounded to start the week ahead!

Please note: this is a paid women's circle; the ticket cost is $10. Pay by Venmo or cash at the start of the circle.

Hosted by Yulia Denisyuk, a veteran [travel journalist](https://www.yulia-denisyuk.com/), host of the [Going Places platform](https://goingplacesmedia.com/), and teacher who's traveled to over 100 countries in search of wisdom. During a women's circle at the Temple of Moon in Peru, Yulia felt the call to continue these gatherings back home – and she followed the call.

This is not a yoga session. This is a gathering for women to practice gentle meditation, mindfulness, stretching, and a few yoga poses meant to activate our intuition and inner wisdom.

Practical info:
\- The session will last about 1 hour\, with about 10 minutes before and after to prep and wind down\. Total time: \~ 1 hour and 10 minutes
\- Bring your own yoga mat or a blanket to sit on\.
\- The session will be on the shore of Lake Michigan in Lakeview\. We'll gather in a shaded\, tree\-lined part of the shore\.

long_description:

***sign up at https://www.riograndesierraclub.org/calendar/***
Every day, the weather feels more and more like summer! Trees are leafing and flowers are blooming! Time to think about summer and heading into the Sandias! So, we're thinking about plans for the Annual Sierra Club Picnic! Sierra Club members and friends are invited to join us for a potluck of yummy offerings, plus panoramic views, bird watching, fresh air and sunshine!

Here are the details:
**When:** July 25, 2026, 10 am to 2 pm
**Where:** *Capulin Springs Picnic Area in the Cibola National Forest*. For details, visit [http:www.rec.gov ](http://http:www.rec.gov)
Some highlights - This picnic site is surrounded by heavily wooded land that affords shade to escape the heat of the day. The spring at Capulin Spring runs year-round and is a much visited spot by birders, especially in the dry season because thirsty birds flock to this area for a nice, cool drink of water. Bring a potluck offering to share.

*If your last name starts with A-H, bring a main entree; last name starts with I-S, appetizers and salads; last name starts with T-Z, dessert. Drinks, chips, plates, utensils and napkins will be provided by the Central Group.*

Bring a friend!

***sign up at https://www.riograndesierraclub.org/calendar/***

title: Saturday Morning Yoga + Park Cleanup!

Homies! This yoga class on Saturdays at 10am will be followed by a park cleanup each week. After ten years of teaching at Leahi Park it is long overdue to give back to the community and the park. At the end of the 10-11am yoga class, Homies that are able to stay will join me in picking up trash at Leahi Park and neighboring Makalei Park.

long_description:
Join our group for a guided meditation!

The event begins with a short introductory talk on Buddhism. This is followed by a guided Vajrayana Buddhist meditation. The meditation generally lasts \~20 minutes, and it is accessible and beneficial to people of all experience levels. You are welcome to stay afterwards to ask any questions or talk further.

We will have meditation cushions available, but you are welcome to bring your own if you like. Chairs can also be made available for those who need them.

What Is Buddhist Meditation?

In Buddhism, meditation means "effortlessly remaining in what is". This state may be brought about by calming and holding the mind, when compassion and wisdom are realized, or by working with our bodies' energy channels and meditating on light forms of Buddhas.

About Us

Diamond Way Buddhist Center Chicago belongs to an international non-profit network of over 600 lay Diamond Way Buddhist centers of the Karma Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism, founded by Lama Ole Nydahl and under the spiritual guidance of H.H. the 17th Gyalwa Karmapa, Trinley Thaye Dorje.

Diamond Way Buddhism offers practical and effective methods to realize mind’s inherent richness for the benefit of all. With an accessible and modern style, it works with people’s confidence and desire, using every situation in life to develop fearlessness and joy. We always present a basic introduction for newcomers, and the meditations are guided in English.

To learn more about our center visit:
http://www.diamondway.org/chicago/

\*This event is free. Just come as you are and enjoy.

Start the week off right with our Sunday night kirtan meditation, and vegetarian dinner! This program is a great way to relax, focus inward, and spend time getting to know others who are interested in making positive changes in their lives.

Kirtan is a clearly guided, group meditation practice using yoga mantras accompanied by live acoustic music. It is a relaxing and centering practice which leaves one in a peaceful condition of mind and heart.
Everything for the meal is provided. Meals will almost always be fully vegan. We accept donations if you would like to help us cover the costs of putting on the events, but there is no obligation. All of our events are FREE.

Our location will be easily accessible from the Sugar House Garden Center Building parking lot right off of 2100 S, as well as the community garden within Sugar House Park.
From the Garden Center Building, walk south behind the center for a couple hundred yards and you will see us set up in the grass. There will also be a "Meditation SLC" banner that will be visible as you approach.
From the community garden and the road within Sugar House Park, keep your eye out for the van with the "Meditation SLC" banner on it, park by the community garden and walk to the east behind the garden for about a hundred yards. Look for another "Meditation SLC" banner at our location. The community garden is on the east side of the Sugar House Park, just past the Highland High School ball fields and up the small hill.

long_description:
Flow Beneath the Bells: Traditional Yoga at the Netherlands Carillon

Cost: Free
Level: Beginner Friendly

Take a break from the noise and join us for a refreshing hour of yoga in one of Arlington’s most beautiful outdoor spaces.

Whether you’ve been practicing for years or can’t touch your toes without negotiating first, you’re welcome here. This class is designed for beginners, but experienced practitioners will also enjoy the flow.

During this session we’ll:

• Learn foundational yoga poses
• Explore simple breathing techniques to reduce stress and improve focus
• Build strength, balance, and flexibility
• Stretch out tight muscles from work, running, cycling, or life in general
• Spend an hour moving, breathing, and reconnecting with ourselves

No pressure. No competition. No yoga experience required.

What to Bring

• A yoga mat or large towel
• Water
• Comfortable clothes you can move in
• An open mind

A Few Quick Notes

• Please arrive a few minutes early so we can start on time.
• Avoid a heavy meal right before class. Light snacks are fine.
• If your plans change, please update your RSVP so someone else can join.

long_description:
### **🔥 Sunday Fire Circle — Queen's Beach Park (by Barefoot Beach Cafe)**

**Always free. Always open to watchers. No pressure, no cost — just come.**
End your weekend the way it deserves to end. We gather on the grass at Queen's Beach Park, right by Barefoot Beach Cafe, where the sun sets behind Waikiki and the ocean keeps time. Grab a coffee or a bite from Barefoot, find a soft patch of grass, and settle in.
This is O'ahu's cross-disciplinary movement arts community — fire dancers, poets, musicians, DJs, yogis, holistic facilitators, and friends. Come spin. Come share a piece. Come stretch, drum, sing, or just witness the circle come alive against the dusk.

**The Flow of the Night**

* **One hour before sunset** — Classes & skill shares. Beginner-friendly intros to poi, staff, fans, and safe spinning. Props to borrow, teachers ready.
* **Sunset** — The circle opens. Fire goes up, music comes on, the night begins. If you aren't spinning fire you are encouraged to dance to the music regardless!
* **9 PM** — Last burn. We pack out together.

**What to Bring (if you're spinning)**

* Natural fiber clothing (cotton or wool — no synthetics near flame)
* Water + a layer for after dark
* Your prop, instrument, mic, or mat
* A small light for setup and breakdown

**Just watching?** Bring yourself. Maybe a blanket. That's it.
**Before You Spin: Sign the Waiver**
Anyone stepping into the circle to spin needs to complete our waiver. Two minutes, online: **[https://www.trialbyfire.community/fire-circle](https://www.trialbyfire.community/fire-circle)**
**Community Guidelines**

* **Consent first** — ask before you touch, photograph, or enter someone's space.
* **Substance-free** — Strictly no alcohol, no cocaine, no ketamine.
* **The circle is working space** — stay outside the perimeter unless you're spinning, fueling, or on safety.
* **Respect the fuel, props, and people.**
* **Leave it better than you found it.**

**RSVP if you can — helps us plan props and safeties. New h

long_description:
*Because training should be as joyful as race day*
Join us for a light-hearted, tail-wagging training series leading up to the Where the Pavement Ends Single Loop Canicross trail race in Ridgefield, CT on September 20. Whether you're running, walking, or trotting beside your pup, this biweekly Sunday meetup is designed to help both humans and dogs build confidence, endurance, and connection—without taking ourselves too seriously.
\#\#\# ✨ What to Expect
We’ll begin each session with a **short walk** to calm our minds and center our bond with our dogs and maybe hug a couple of trees. Think deep breaths, paws on the earth, and the simple joy of being outside together.
Then we’ll ease into:

* Gentle warm-up walks
* Playful agility & leash work
* Trail runs or power walks (we’ll build distance gradually)
* Social time for dogs and humans
* 🐶 Who’s Welcome

All friendly dogs and their human teammates—runners, walkers, hikers, beginners, and seasoned adventure buddies. No race experience required. (Puppies must be fully vaccinated.)

\#\#\# 🥾 What to Bring

* Water
* Leash (no retractables, please)
* High-value treats
* A sense of humor

This isn’t just training—it’s community. By September, we’ll be more than ready for race day… and probably have a lot of muddy paw prints on our hearts. And if you don't want to register for the event and just want to come out for the fun and exercise, please do!!

* To learn more about the race please visit https://runsignup.com/Race/CT/Ridgefield/WherethePavementEnds?raceRefCode=su8FTWDR

I have been studying, training and teaching yoga for over 25 years. I want to help serve others by sharing this powerful tradition. I work with seniors as well as teenagers. I am a Yoga Teacher E-RYT500 as well as trained Yoga Therapist with the International Association of Yoga Therapy.
I was planning on going back to school to get a PhD in Yoga Science and Ayurveda, but my teacher told me that if I needed to start teaching. He said that in this tradition, if you don't teach what you have learned in yoga to others, it is considered stealing.
So, I have been sharing and teaching ever since now for many years. I have loads of information and can share a multitude of practices to help with any specific need or condition (physical, physiological, mental/ emotional/ spiritual ).
The goal of yoga is to reduce suffering on all levels (physical, energetic, mental/emotional, find joy, and BECOME FREE! SPEAKING OF FREE, I offer 4 free community yoga classes a week each Monday and Wednesday for Eastbluff Community. Please consider joining a class or two, meet your neighbors, have some fun, and increase your longevity, health span, and overall wellness and connect to the joy that resides within your heart ❤️. For more details you can contact me here or email me at janet@heartofyoga.com

long_description:
Traditional yoga taught by former Tibetan Buddhist monk Balto Sultimov.
His journey in yoga began at 25 years old when he was paralyzed on half of his body due to a stroke, where a local coach taught yoga twice a day in which Balto committed himself to 2.5 months of daily practice leading to reversing all of the damage from the stroke and achieving full recovery.
This experience brought him to go to Rishikesh India, a place considered the "Birthplace of Yoga" and "Yoga Capital of the World."
Balto teaches about the subtle fascia muscle, basic yoga posture, and a traditional series of asanas . His philosophy is in gentle feeling and easing into stretches rather than forcefulness.

long_description:

**Classes are gentle and breath centric. Poses are adapted to meet your needs. Regardless of your age, health, condition, if you can breath you can do yoga!! Increase your strength, flexibility, balance, energy, mental focus, and overall feelings of well-being and joy! Classes are free or donation based. Join the community, meet new connections while growing younger. Please RSVP or email me at janet@atheartofyoga,com for more details.**

### **Yoga is a journey. We can take that journey together, and it can be your guide for life. Yoga is NOT an aesthetic practice of aspiration. It is a practice to reclaim your joy and develop your physical and mental resilience.**

### **Let 2023 be the year to let go of old patterns that hold you back from wellness, and make space for what is most precious; wellness in body, mind, heart, soul, and the abundance of joy and friendships.**

### **The ancient practices of yoga and meditation cultivates wisdom and wellness and a caravan in which we move through all of life's joys and struggles. Yoga is the most ancient, deepest, and potent of medicines.**

### **And the good news is that ANYONE can practice yoga. If you are breathing. ..You can do yoga! Regular practice promises the reduction of suffering (Dukha) and brings health to body, peace to your heart, and joy in heart.**

### **As the great Sri K Patabhi Jois says "Practice and all is coming" The ancient practices of yoga and meditation cultivates wisdom and wellness and a caravan in which we move through all of life's joys and struggles.**

### **It is a true joy to share the teachings of yoga. Over the years I have witnesses so much healing, joy, in my students, as well as the friendships and connections made.**

### **Wishing you an abundance of health, courage, inspiration and blessings in the year ahead!**

### **Namaste🙏,**

### **Janet Marshall**

long_description:
Open Recovery Meetings offer a supportive, judgment-free space for people at any point in their relationship with substances—whether you’re sober, actively using, in recovery, or simply curious about change.
These gatherings are rooted in the belief that real healing happens in community and that we are not meant to do this work alone.

Facilitated by Kate and Lorren, this meeting is led by two people with lived experience. One facilitator is a peer support professional and the other is currently working toward peer support certification, both holding lengths of sustained sobriety. Together, they hold space with honesty, humility, compassion, and heart—creating an environment where people can show up as they are.

Each meeting offers time to share, listen, and connect through real stories and mutual support. There is no requirement to identify in any particular way, no expectation to “have it all figured out,” and no pressure to participate beyond what feels right for you.
This is an open, welcoming space grounded in respect, care, and shared humanity.

While no space is perfect, the intention here is to foster connection, reduce isolation, and support one another through lived experience and community care.
Come as you are. You don’t have to do this alone.

***\*\*\*DISCLAIMER\*\*\****
The Karma House offers an alcohol free, harm reduction centered environment for those in recovery which primarily serves the botanical beverages Kava and Kratom. As with any substance you choose to consume, we encourage folks to do their own research and to ask the Kava tenders any other questions you may have to determine if these drinks are right for you and your recovery journey! We also have a variety of herbal teas and nootropic beverages available!

long_description:
Let's have another book club on the beach! We will meet in Lewes June!

For anyone who hasn't joined in Lewes, we will meet on the corner of the large parking lot. We walk together to go get ice cream, go back and grab our chairs/blankets to sit on, and get settled on the beach after that.

**Book:**
The Unhoneymooners by Christina Lauren

**About:**
Olive is always unlucky: in her career, in love, in…well, everything. Her identical twin sister Ami, on the other hand, is probably the luckiest person in the world. Her meet-cute with her fiancé is something out of a romantic comedy (gag) and she’s managed to finance her entire wedding by winning a series of Internet contests (double gag). Worst of all, she’s forcing Olive to spend the day with her sworn enemy, Ethan, who just happens to be the best man. Olive braces herself to get through 24 hours of wedding hell before she can return to her comfortable, unlucky life. But when the entire wedding party gets food poisoning from eating bad shellfish, the only people who aren’t affected are Olive and Ethan. And now there’s an all-expenses-paid honeymoon in Hawaii up for grabs. Putting their mutual hatred aside for the sake of a free vacation, Olive and Ethan head for paradise, determined to avoid each other at all costs. But when Olive runs into her future boss, the little white lie she tells him is suddenly at risk to become a whole lot bigger. She and Ethan now have to pretend to be loving newlyweds, and her luck seems worse than ever. But the weird thing is that she doesn’t mind playing pretend. In fact, she feels kind of... lucky.

description:
For over a year now, we have been hosting a networking night every Tuesday at the Capitalist Club Coworking Lounge in Costa Mesa and we are finally happy to expand here into the Meetup ecosystem.

On average we have 30–40 entrepreneurs, business owners, and professionals in the facility each week. It’s not a typical mixer. I’ve found that the best connections don’t come from forced introductions — they happen through shared experiences.
That’s why our nights revolve around doing things together.
long_description:
For over a year now, we have been hosting a networking night every Tuesday at the Capitalist Club Coworking Lounge in Costa Mesa and we are finally happy to expand here into the Meetup ecosystem.

On average we have 30–40 entrepreneurs, business owners, and professionals in the facility each week. It’s not a typical mixer. I’ve found that the best connections don’t come from forced introductions — they happen through shared experiences.
That’s why our nights revolve around doing things together.
You can jump into the poker game, shoot pool, hit balls on the golf simulator, play air hockey, enjoy a cigar in the outdoor area, or just grab a drink and connect with people.

The cost is $120 for the day pass at the Capitalist Club (Members are Free) Which includes dinner, drinks and $100 in credits to play poker or try your skill at the Hole in one Challenge or the Run The Rack Challenge.

I structure it this way intentionally because when people invest in being here the room changes — and so does the level of conversation. It also weeds out the freeloaders.

If you’re local, have value to give and appreciate real relationships over surface-level networking, you’ll fit in here.
I look forward to meeting and collaborating with everyone.
Cheers, Semper Fi
Matt

P.S. if this is your first event you'll have to fill out the [Capitalist Club Guest Profile](https://joz5hnsou0rn33id-89945604385.shopifypreview.com/pages/customer-form) which you are welcome to do when you arrive or before hand with that link to save time.

long_description:
**ABOUT THE THIRD OPTION PROGRAM**

The Third Option is a group program to build better relationships. It is designed for all people and can be used as enrichment for healthy couples who want to enhance their relationship, or as crisis intervention for couples who are separated or considering divorce.

This class combines skill-building workshops with sharing from couples that have “been there”, and a support group component. The atmosphere is warm and caring.

**WHAT IS “THE THIRD OPTION?”**

For a couple who is struggling, Option 1 is to stay miserable in an unhappy relationship, and Option 2 is to get out – divorce. “The Third Option” is to learn the skills needed to have a happy and healthy relationship. If even one partner wants to work at the relationship, they can come alone, and the relationship will benefit. It's better yet if both partners attend.

**WHEN DO THE CLASSES OCCUR?**

This ongoing class meets every Tuesday evening from 6:30 to 8:30pm. The Third Option operates on a 14 week cycle that restarts again after the last week, so it’s continuous. This means it is OK to join at any time.

There is no charge to attend the first two weeks; after that there is a suggested donation of $10 per person, per week (if finances are a problem, come anyway! No one is ever turned away by lack of funds). There's no need to sign up ahead of time, and the group keeps confidentiality about who attends and what is shared.

**WHERE DO THE CLASSES MEET?**

English - North Orange County – Tuesdays, 6:30pm-8:30pm

long_description:
Come to receive a session of Light Energy. Sessions are 15-60 minutes depending on your schedule and preference. There is no cost, but spiritual offerings to the Sukyo Mahikari (http://sukyomahikari.org/) organization are welcomed.

Why receive Light?

Various spiritual principles underlie the natural world. Sometimes it is easy to practice the universal principles, but sometimes even people who want to live in harmony with their innate spirituality encounter situations where they do not know how to apply the universal principles. For example, people may find themselves in a job or relationship that makes them unhappy or which hinders them from accomplishing their goals. When tools for spiritual growth are practiced together with experiencing light energy, people can more quickly attain personal growth and help make the world a better place.

What is Light?

Energy that purifies the spiritual aspect of people and all things. Light can be radiated to anything – food, animals, plants, homes, workplaces, cars, and so on. By purifying their surroundings with this energy, many people notice that their surroundings become more pleasant and often appear brighter. This helps everyone around them gradually become more connected with their spirituality and to start to think more about how to live in harmony with their fellow human beings and the environment.

Where can you read more about it?

"True Light: Ordinary People on the Extraordinary Spiritual Path of Sukyo Mahikari" was recently published.

No doubt AI is changing a lot about our economy, techno
long_description:
Join us this month for a fascinating and timely fireside chat with a power-packed panel of startup community builders, moderated by COED's Jonathan Chambers on AI and Community, "Human Advantage: Why Community Still Wins in the Age of AI", featuring Julie Pierre, Community & Ecosystem Development at Tech Square; Nisha Kavalam, Vice President of Operations & Marketing of Atlanta Tech Week; Ania Lackey, Executive Director of FinTech Atlanta.

No doubt AI is changing a lot about our economy, technology, culture, and how we do business. Even how we interact and relate to each other in community. But, has it replaced and redefined what it means to be a community and build a thriving community within that AI-driven economy? Hear from some of Atlanta's top innovation leaders and startup community builders at the cusp of technology, AI, and startups and how they continue to keep the human element strong and present in building a thriving, connected, and innovative community.

Whether you're in tech, startups, community, and any level of AI use, you'll leave with fresh reminders of the power of the human advantage of community in the age of AI.

organizer: A Cappella Singers and Vocalists of Upstate NY
long_description:
Men of the New York State Capital District with a desire to sing in an accomplished chorus are invited to join the chorus and take advantage of our excellent leadership and instruction. The Electric City Chorus is a men’s a cappella vocal music group singing in the Barbershop Style. We strive to sing at the highest quality, to entertain, and to experience great fellowship and enjoyment.

You do not have to be a great singer; you just need to be a guy who likes to sing, and willing to learn. You do not have to be able to sing your part alone; you will be singing with the chorus. If you have ever sung in the shower or found yourself singing along with the music on the radio, chances are you will enjoy singing with us. If you are a little nervous about the whole idea, bring a friend along for moral (and vocal) support!

Visit one of our rehearsals and check us out. You won't be pressured to join, but you will have a lot of fun singing with us.

The ECC meets every Tuesday at 7:00 PM at Schenectady Light Opera's Performing Arts Center (enter at 418 Liberty Street in Schenectady), unless we are out singing somewhere in the community. For more information email: manager@electriccitychorus.net; visit our website at: https://www.electriccitychorus.net/, or see us on Facebook, at: https://www.facebook.com/ElectricCityChorus/

The Electric City Chorus is a member of the international barbershop organization, the Barbershop Harmony Society, in the Northeast District (NED).

The ECC sings at many community venues in all seasons of the year. In addition, the chorus periodically competes and sings with other choruses in the northeast section of the United States and eastern Canada.

long_description:
Breathe deeply, touch the earth, look up at the sky.

This summer and through September, we are taking our practice out of the studio and into the fresh air. Join us for outdoor sessions designed to help you ground your energy, build strength, and connect with the community in our beautiful local green spaces. All levels are welcome, from complete beginners to experienced practitioners.

Practicing outdoors is wonderful, but it does require a tiny bit of extra preparation. Here is what you should bring to get the most out of your session:

* A Yoga Mat or Large Towel
* Water
* Optional: yoga blocks and strap
* Arrive a few minutes early to find your spot and settle in.

Please also register in advance with the Town of Windsor [here](https://secure.rec1.com/CT/town-windsor/catalog/index/e56fcd7931ad028f636d7158daa218ed?filter=c2VhcmNoPUZyYW5r).

Yoga is a way to get to know our bodies better, calm our ever-thinking minds and enjoy some inner peace. Treat yourself to 90 minutes self-care. Leave class refreshed and rejuvenated! Feel free to leave questions in the comments section or message me on meetup.

Class includes breath-work, postures, correct alignment, relaxation, meditation, and yogic wisdom. Modifications to postures are suggested to accommodate individual needs.

Our bodies are unique so beginners are encouraged to take their time and adapt slowly to the postures, resting as they deem appropriate for their bodies. Props such as chairs, blocks, straps, bolsters and blankets are available in studio to assist you.

Yoga is a practice that cultivates joy, concentration, mindfulness, body awareness, flexibility, health and serenity. Simply put, yoga is fun. It is not a sequence of masochistic exercises!

This does not mean we practice yoga haphazardly. Quite the contrary. We bring body, breath, mental focus and magnanimous spirit to every asana (posture.) We are fully present . . . but without strain, tension, self-judgment or perfectionism.

My name is Frank .

long_description:
PyHawaii will be having a meeting at the end of July with two talks this month. The first talk will be by Andrew Vogel about engineering failures and running post-mortems.

"Engineering failures don't have a single cause. We build layered systems with safeguards at every level, and it takes multiple issues stacking up to build a public-facing failure. Blameless post-mortems are critical to finding all these failures. Testing assumptions a the most granular level you can fit within business needs is critical to successful blameless post-mortems."

I will also give a talk on memray ( https://github.com/bloomberg/memray ). Memray is a memory profiler that allows you to track and observe memory allocations in python and determine what is causing excessive memory usage. This talk will be a brief intro to using memray.

About the speaker:
Andrew is a Stanford graduate that's worked previously with Trimble, VMWare, Nest/Google Home, and RenewHome. He's worked extensively on orchestration frameworks and end-to-end testing of software systems.

long_description:
Mantra Yoga

Mantra Yoga is a meditative sound practice that activates healing, clarity, and awareness through the vibration of your own voice. Whether spoken, whispered, or chanted, each mantra becomes a tool for transformation.

In this class, we explore the pronunciation, meaning, and energy of sacred mantras. You may have heard them in Kundalini Yoga or other tradition and held back—this is your chance to deepen into their sound and fully experience their power.

Each session evolves organically, beginning with guided recitation, followed by call-and-response chanting, and devotional sound journeys. You’ll be supported by live harmonium, and from time to time, guest musicians who bring added depth to the experience.

Even if it’s your first time, all you need is an open heart. You’ll leave feeling lighter, more connected, and empowered by the vibration that lives within you.

Benefits include:
• Calms the mind and relieves anxiety
• Clears subconscious patterns and emotional blocks
• Strengthens vocal confidence and breath control
• Activates energy centers (chakras)
• Increases mental focus and inner peace
• Deepens meditation and devotional awareness
• Uplifts the spirit and fosters joy
• Awaken the power of your own voice.

A journey into healing sound, sacred words, and the vibration of consciousness. Let your voice lead the way. All levels welcome.

long_description:
**🌐 CONNECTED BY WIRE, APART BY HEART**
We have more ways to connect than any generation in history—yet loneliness has become one of the defining challenges of our time.
Join a world-traveling swami for an inspiring evening exploring the ancient yoga wisdom that helps us cultivate genuine connection in an age of deep disconnection.
We swipe, scroll, and double-tap through thousands of lives every day, yet many of us feel unseen, unheard, and alone.
**📊 The numbers tell the story:**
• Nearly half of young adults report experiencing loneliness
• Many of us check our phones 100+ times a day, mistaking stimulation for connection
• More people than ever report having few—or no—close friends they can rely on
✨ **Swami on Overcoming Loneliness** is not a self-help seminar or a lecture. It is an invitation to step away from the noise and explore a deeper understanding of connection, belonging, and fulfillment.
Drawing from timeless yoga philosophy, the swami will share practical insights into why we feel disconnected, how the mind creates separation, and what we can do to experience authentic relationships—with others and ourselves.
**🧘 The Evening Includes:**
• Insightful talk on overcoming loneliness and cultivating meaningful connection
• Guided meditation for inner stillness
• Restorative sound bath for deep relaxation
• Nourishing vegan dinner shared in community
🌿 For one evening, put down the phone, step into the room, and experience a different kind of connection.
You may leave with more than inspiration—you may leave with a new way of relating to yourself and the world around you.

This is an invitation specifically for persons who identify as Black or African American and are overwhelmed with the injustice of the world and are ready to create space in their lives for self-care as we fight for justice for all! We believe Black people deserve a space to relax, reassess, and realign ourselves.

We are a collective of Black stress-management & wellness instructors inspired by human values.

We are here to facilitate your journey of trauma-relief and stress-management.

Imagine how much more energy you will have and how much more powerful you will be when you cut your stress levels in half!

And it can be done in just a few minutes using nothing but your own breath...

Over the last 10 years, we've taught over 100,000 people to do just that.
The key is that your breath is directly linked to your emotions.

-Breath work and meditation

Led by Black facilitators, certified in stress and trauma relief.

Ever wonder how the Downward Dog walks? Join us as we dive in to the wild world of animal movement! We will learn to move with fluid integration, open up space in the body, and flex our imaginations.

long_description:
Bring your yoga mat, blanket, and any other comfort items as you will be laying down for this deeply healing session.
Transformational Breathwork is a powerful ACTIVE breathing meditation for self-healing. This practice appeals especially to people who enjoy yoga, as it addresses the mind, body, and spirit of the individual.
You will be learning a 2 stage 'pranayama yoga' breath, which is the active portion of the practice, and sometimes called the 'work' part of breathwork. The active breathing segment is followed by an integration, or rest period. This is all done to specific music while lying down on a yoga mat. Bolsters, blankets are recommended, eye masks are provided.

This is a specific, rhythmic breathing pattern that can help clear out emotions and stuck energy. It literally quiets the mind so that the heart can open and heal. A modality that must be experienced to appreciate.

This is a RWJ Community Event.

$15 per person
Call 609-584-5900 to register.

long_description:
**YOGA AT THE BLUFFS**
**INTEGRATIVE HEALT AND WELLNESS**
**FOR SUCCESFUL AGING**
FREE YOGA CLASSES !

Just as there is a science and technology to create external well-being, there is a whole dimension since and technology for inner well-being - and that is yoga!

Increase your vitality, resiliency, physical strength and flexibility, energy, stabilize your mind, calm your emotions and find joy in your life. Yoga practice will help you manage your energy, sleep better, eat better, have better relationships and help you to feel more ease and happiness in your life. This is the promise of yoga.

My classes are held every Monday and Wednesday mornings in Newport Beach at Eastbluff Clubhouse: 2490 Vista del Oro. Class times are from 10am-11:20am. Classes are gentle and appropriate for the perfect beginner, or strong practitioner, and FREE or donation based!

Classes are breath centric, and adapted to your needs, age, lifestyle, and condition. I am a yoga teacher and yoga therapist certified through International Association of Yoga Therapy. I trained for over 20 years in several traditions but teach in the Viniyoga tradition of Krishnamacharya. I teach all ages but my particular focus in teaching seniors (ages 55-105).

Poses are adapted for your individual need. We practice poses to increase strength, flexibility, ROM, balance, focus, and concentration. The breath work increases vitality and health of all your systems; cardiovascular, respiratory, circulatory, immune, and digestive. Class is followed by meditation to help stabilize the mind and emotions, and bring one to state of inner light and joy.

Please bring a mat, a smile, and an open curious mind. You deserve to be healthy, happy, and whole, and the practices of yoga guide you towards better overall health and wellbeing. An added benefit of these classes is that you will meet some very nice people.

If interested you can email me at janet@heartofyoga.com or respond on meetup.

May you be happy and well!
Janet M

long_description:
SIGN UP via link: https://clients.mindbodyonline.com/asp/main_enroll.asp

This is a 60 minute somatic based workshop designed to help participants slow down, reconnect with their body, and better understand the patterns driving stress, overwhelm, anxiety, emotional shutdown, and disconnection.
The workshop blends guided somatic meditation, nervous system understanding and regulation, breathwork, gentle movement, and restorative yoga in a way that feels approachable, grounding, and safe for all levels.
We begin with grounding practices and guided breathwork to help participants settle into the body and regulate the nervous system. From there, I lead the group through a somatic meditation experience where participants begin noticing physical sensations, tension patterns, emotions, and the thoughts connected to them.
A large part of the workshop focuses on helping people understand how the nervous system shapes emotional patterns, stress responses, self criticism, overthinking, and the beliefs we carry about ourselves. The goal is not to “fix” anything, but to create awareness, safety, and reconnection within the body.
The restorative yoga and movement portion is intentionally gentle and supportive rather than performance based. It’s designed to help participants release stored tension, soften out of stress mode, and leave feeling more grounded and connected to themselves.
The overall tone is very calming, safe, reflective, and beginner friendly while still offering emotional depth and practical tools people can apply in daily life.
This is a good fit for people who are interested in yoga, healing, stress relief, nervous system work, mindfulness, emotional wellness, or simply slowing down and reconnecting with themselves in a deeper way.

SIGN UP via link: https://clients.mindbodyonline.com/asp/main_enroll.asp

long_description:
## **Yin Yoga Flow**

**Find Stillness. Release Tension. Restore Flow.'**

In a world that values constant movement, the **Yin Yoga Flow** is your invitation to slow down and turn inward. This practice targets the deeper "yin" tissues of the body - the fascia, ligaments, and joints rather than the superficial muscles, offering a profound sense of physical and mental release.
Unlike a traditional vinyasa class, this session focuses on long-held, passive floor poses, allowing the body to naturally open and the nervous system to shift into a state of deep rest.

### **The Practice**

* **Targeted Release:** Hold postures for 3–5 minutes to access connective tissues and improve joint mobility.
* **Mindful Presence:** Use the stillness to practice meditative awareness, observing sensations and thoughts without judgment.
* **Subtle Energy Flow:** Clear blockages in the body’s meridians to restore a sense of equilibrium and vitality.
* **Gentle Transitions:** Poses are linked with slow, intentional transitions to maintain a meditative state from start to finish.

### **Class Benefits**

* **Deep Flexibility:** Increases circulation and suppleness in the hips, pelvis, and lower spine.
* **Stress Reduction:** Activates the parasympathetic nervous system (rest and digest) to lower cortisol levels.
* **Mental Clarity:** Provides a quiet space to decompress and regulate your emotional engine.

**Best For:** All levels. Whether you are an athlete looking to recover or simply need a break from the digital noise, this class is your sanctuary.
**Leave feeling: Grounded, spacious, and deeply renewed.**

Donation Based: ($5-$25 Sliding Scale)

long_description:
Let’s hang out at Thompson's Point for [Summer Sunsets Live](https://thompsonspoint.com/things-to-do/summer-sunsets/) with all the summer good stuff: Live music, beautiful scenery, food trucks, local cocktails and brews. Entry is **free** and you can also **carry-in picnic** food! Make sure to bring a picnic blanket or chair; we'll sit together in the grass. This event is on-leash **dog-friendly and kid friendly**. Thompson's Point does NOT let people carry-in drinks, alcohol or non-alcohol. There a place to fill a water bottle if you bring an empty one.

The food truck lines can be long. It's usually easier to just bring food in, or just plan accordingly if you're ordering from a food truck.

The band playing and food truck line-up is TBA - Thompson's Point will announce them on Instagram when the event gets closer. I'll try to update here when that happens. This event is outdoors so **weather permitting**.

**Finding us**: I'll post a comment on the event when I arrive so you know how to find us. It's a big area, but I'll be as descriptive as possible, so make sure to check here for that info. DM me if you can't find us.

**Getting there**: Walking or biking is encouraged. There are buses that go to Thompson's Point too. If you need to drive, please be aware that the parking lot is pay-to-park 24/7!

Stay home if you're feeling ill or exposed to someone sick.

long_description:
Hi SD:DC!
Join Service Design DC and our friends at MediaBarn for our annual Summer Social, a relaxed evening dedicated to connection, conversation, and community.

**This is your chance to:**

* Meet fellow service design practitioners, students, and enthusiasts from across the DMV.
* Swap stories about current projects, sticky challenges, and ideas you are eager to test.
* Find your next collaborator, mentor, mentee, hiring manager, or future teammate.

We will have light, low-pressure activities (including our fan-favorite Service Design Bingo) to help break the ice and spark meaningful conversations, but the focus of the night is networking and building relationships.

Whether you are looking to get hired, hiring for your team, sharing an idea, or simply curious about service design, you are welcome. Bring a friend or coworker, come as you are, and stay for the energy of a community that loves designing better services together.

**Evening Agenda**
6:00 P.M. - Doors Open + Socializing
6:30 P.M. - SD:DC and Sponsor introductions
6:40 P.M. - Networking Activities (Service Design Bingo, and others)
7:45 P.M. - Winners & wrap up

**Many thanks to our host and sponsor, MediaBarn!**

*Mediabarn’s customer-centric philosophy defines who we are.*
*In its simplest form, we are committed to applying Human-Centered Design (HCD) methods to understand customer needs, collect feedback, and use that feedback to improve services and products. Whether it’s for customers, citizens, or employees, our Experience Design Studio creates research-informed designs to improve the experience of every human involved.*

long_description:
Here's the agenda for this Meetup:

Please note we will start promptly at 12:00 pm. Please be a few minutes early so you will have time to order some lunch. Also, give yourself a few minutes to catch up with other members. This will ensure that we can start on time and then we will be able to leave on time.
We do ask that as we get back to in-person networking, you WILL NEED

• We'll do a brief introduction of ABNG and also quickly go over our rules (don't worry, there's only three and a half!). Then, we'll get right to the meeting.

• Hold on to your business cards for now. We will start the meeting by going around the room with our introductions. Notice we didn't say 30-second commercial or elevator pitch. There's a fantastic TED talk ([https://youtu.be/u4ZoJKF_VuA](https://youtu.be/u4ZoJKF_VuA)) from Simon Sinek that might blow you away.

• After introductions, we'll do our shoutouts and share our member events. If you had a great 1:1 with someone or have some other awesome thing to share, we have the space for that! If you have a workshop, class, meeting or event coming up, this is a great time to inform the group. We will also discuss specific needs you may have. Do you need a resource of some kind? Chances are someone in our group can point you in the right direction.

• If time allows, we will engage in our Mastermind discussion. If you feel like you have something in your business that is holding you back, this is time and the place to tackle it. If you have something that you need help with, make sure to let the host know before the meeting starts so that we can make time for it during our meeting. The power of the group is immense!

• We'll close out our meeting by passing around business cards and ensuring you have time to set up your 1:1's before adjourning at 1:00 p.m.
We look forward to seeing you at our next meeting!

long_description:
Let's enjoy some Malaysian food at Food Terminal. This will be our first Malaysian food event and I think this is the perfect restaurant to do it at.

Food Terminal’s concept reflects Malaysia’s diverse culinary cuisine.

Food Terminal showcases a vibrant mix of Asian street food, with a special emphasis on authentic Malaysian cuisine. Its menu highlights a rich selection of dishes inspired by the bold flavors and culinary traditions of Indian and Chinese cooking. Together, these influences create a diverse and flavorful dining experience that reflects the true essence of Malaysia’s multicultural food culture.

**Food Terminal Origin Story:**
At age 15, Amy began her culinary path selling street-style noodles from a kiosk in Malaysia. Together with Howie, the duo came to the United States to pursue the American dream as entrepreneurs. Howie and Amy spent decades exploring culinary achievements, creating brands such as Top Spice and Sweet Hut.

Even after years of business accomplishments, the real satisfaction for them is not the success of the restaurants and bakeries, but the appreciation people express after tasting their food.
Inspired by the chefs’ personal cultural background, Food Terminal’s concept reflects Malaysia’s diverse culinary cuisine. Malaysian food draws influence from India, Guang Zhou, Hokkien, Teochew, and Hakka provinces due to the early 1900’s migration for tin and railroad labor demand. As such, Food Terminal’s menu features a high variety of Asian street foods with heavy emphasis on Malaysian cuisine. Food Terminal’s mission is to bring the most authentic Asian-style street taste and experience to Buford Highway.

**A Local Guide's review of Food Terminal:**
Food Terminal boasts an extensive South Asian menu, with a definite Malaysian bent, in a relaxed and informal atmosphere. The food is excellent. Some highlights include:

\- Beef Rendang: one of my favorite renditions of this complex and very flavorful West Sumatran dish
\- Chicken Satay

long_description:
**We will meet in Study Room 2 near the back of the library**

**Feeling isolated or navigating the tender terrain after a relationship ends? You are not alone.** **Join us for** **Quiet Conversations: Our Haven for Connection****, a warm and welcoming space designed for genuine support and understanding.**

**We gather bi-weekly at the Glendale Branch Library. This isn't just a meetup; it's a place to find your footing, share your journey, and build meaningful connections with others who truly understand.**

**Whether you're newly separated, years post-divorce, or simply looking to expand your supportive circle, this peer-led group offers a haven to feel seen, heard, and deeply supported.** **Please note: This is a peer-led community, not a therapy or coaching group. It's a space for shared experience and mutual encouragement, not professional mental health support.**

**Your Contribution to Our Haven:** **This community thrives on the spirit of mutual support. Many members have expressed how invaluable these gatherings are, and some have even offered to contribute financially. To help us continue providing this vital space and cover Meetup fees and other community resources, we welcome your support.**

**Suggested Donation: $10 - $20 per session (or whatever feels right for you).** **Your generosity helps us keep things going and the conversations flowing.**

**You can contribute via Venmo: @michaelleavitthwb**

**Ready to find your chosen family?** **If you're also looking for a creative outlet and a deeper dive into music and shared creativity, check out our sister community,** **[Wandering Bards](https://www.meetup.com/wanderingbard)****. It's our primary home for finding your 'shovel friends' through the power of music, storytelling, and continued growth. Explore our events and join the quest!**

long_description:
Socrates Café meets twice a month. Though this may be considered a "philosophical" group, there are no rules as to what is discussed. Usually, the topics revolve around social concerns, morality, and the first principles of things.

Prior to each meeting we vote online for the questions we will discuss. That way, we will have enough time to ruminate on them and have more in-depth conversations. If you RSVP to a meeting, you may post your question in the event comments section below. I'll send out a survey for voting a few days prior to the meetup. We discuss two questions each night. So you will get to cast two votes in the survey.

When we meet, we break into smaller groups of five to seven to discuss the top two vote-getters. Each group discusses one question for around 45-50 minutes, and we then take a short break. After reconvening, each group moves on to its second question.

Hope to see you there!

-Brian

long_description:
**India's Great Mughals: Art, Power, and Opulence**
**Immerse yourself in the golden age of the Mughal Empire. India's Great Mughals: Art, Power, and Opulence celebrates the glorious artistic achievements and grandeur of one of history's great empires.**
**India's Great Mughals includes 200 sumptuous objects—intricate paintings and manuscripts, lavish textiles, architectural elements, metalwork, furniture, arms and armor, dazzling precious stones, and more. Opulent works of art—many made in the imperial workshops—convey the power and tastes of the three most celebrated Mughal emperors: Akbar (r. 1556–1605), Jahangir (r. 1605–27), and Shah Jahan (r. 1628–58). From the tiniest jeweled objects to the monumental wonder of the Taj Mahal, this highly sophisticated and globally connected empire produced treasures of unparalleled splendor and magnificence.**

long_description:
##

*Along with all the usual exhibits there is a special exhibit going on now:*

***Declarative Acts and Revolutionary Actors*** features objects that fueled the revolution and unsung heroes who made independence possible. The exhibition showcases national treasures from Cincinnati Museum Center’s collections, including an original timber and chain from pre-Cincinnati’s Fort Washington, the regimental flag of the 1st Pennsylvania Battalion – one of just 30 Revolutionary War flags still in existence – ***and the document that united a nation, the Declaration of Independence. Cincinnati Museum Center’s Holt Broadside of the Declaration of Independence, dated July 9, 1776, is one of just five known to have endured the past 250 years.***

Because of its extreme scarcity and light sensitivity, it is typically kept in secure, climate-controlled archival. It will only be on display from July 3rd until August 23rd.

If not a member, tickets are $25.00 for adults, $17.50 60+ & kids. If you have a Hamilton County library card, you can also get free passes using the Discovery Pass.

Tickets Includes admission to Children's Museum, Museum of Natural History & Science, and Cincinnati History Museum.

Well go to eat afterward. Restaurant TBD.

long_description:
Whether you're preparing to meet investors, talk to customers, launch your product, or simply want feedback from fellow founders, this meetup is for you.

**Note:** We’re capping this meetup at 30 people. Only 10 spots are available to RSVP on Meetup - feel free to join the waitlist and I’ll approve additional attendees until we reach capacity.

Bring your startup, business idea, MVP, prototype, or side project and give a short pitch. If you have a product, prototype, landing page, or mockup, we encourage you to give a brief demo as well. Demos are encouraged but not required - if you don't have something to show yet, you're still welcome to pitch and receive valuable feedback.

After each pitch (and demo, if applicable), attendees will have the opportunity to ask questions and provide constructive feedback on your messaging, product, and overall approach. Whether you have an established business, an early MVP, or are still validating your idea, you'll gain valuable insights to help you move forward.

After everyone has had a chance to pitch, we'll transition into a casual networking and co-working session. Stick around to continue conversations, exchange ideas, make new connections, or spend some time working alongside other founders.

Whether you're pitching for the first time or the fiftieth - or simply attending to learn - come ready to support fellow entrepreneurs, share your perspective, and connect with other builders in the DC area.

Whether this is your first LONG distance paddle or you’re one of our returning 32-Miler alumni… you’ll love the challenge!

Brunswick Boat Ramp → Violette’s Lock = 32 miles

Meet: 8:30 AM

description:
Just east of Las Vegas lies one of Southern Nevada's most colorful and overlooked landscapes. While Lava Butte is interesting from the ground, its true beauty reveals itself from above in the morning light, where layers of red, yellow, orange, and tan hills create abstract patterns that seem more at home in a painting than the Mojave Desert.

long_description:
Just east of Las Vegas lies one of Southern Nevada's most colorful and overlooked landscapes. While Lava Butte is interesting from the ground, its true beauty reveals itself from above in the morning light, where layers of red, yellow, orange, and tan hills create abstract patterns that seem more at home in a painting than the Mojave Desert.

This event is specifically designed for drone photographers looking to capture a perspective that simply can't be appreciated from ground level. We'll explore the area at a relaxed pace, searching for the best aerial compositions, colorful ridgelines, winding washes, and the unique textures that make Lava Butte such a hidden gem. Whether you're an experienced pilot or just looking to gain more flight time in a spectacular location, this is a great opportunity to photograph one of the most drone-friendly landscapes near Las Vegas.

**MEETUP INFO:**
We will meet at 6:30am at Sunrise Trailhead. This is just a 30 minute drive from Las Vegas (on the east side of the city by Wetlands Park). Please plan accordingly to arrive on time.

From there, we will drive about 20 minutes down Lava Butte Road on a gravel road that is not recommended for low clearance vehicles. However, it does not require 4WD / AWD. Carpooling is available (I personally would have room for 3 passengers).

**MEETUP FEES:**
There are no fees for this event.

**PHYSICAL ACTIVITY:**
There is minimal walking required, as we will drive into Lava Butte and be able to fly right from our vehicles. Those wishing to explore additional viewpoints may choose to walk short distances over uneven desert terrain.

**ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:**
Please ensure your drone is charged, updated, and ready to fly prior to arrival.

If your plans change and you are unable to attend, please be courteous and cancel your RSVP so that someone else can attend.

**DESERT PHOTO EXPLORERS LIABILITY DISCLAIMER AND ASSUMPTION OF RISK:**
By submitting your RSVP and participating in any Desert Photo Ex

long_description:
Hey Poetry Lovers!

This group is on a roll. Here’s the gist:

We meet at the **Capital One Café in Chinatown** from **12pm - 2pm** every other week.

For enrichment, we start by reading and reflecting on a **“published poem”**, suggested by someone in the group. No advance preparation is necessary. But feel free to check out some of the poems we’ve read [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vSyE_wCLQCPHRrKmN5F9tOIeeRQUZESxjRXGVBoCF2uU8Gm0_d0uECiCBCQXEy6ksxfsBOhtRIOpW3T/pubhtml?gid=0&single=true&widget=true&headers=false%22%3E%3C/iframe%3E). Or submit suggestions for future meetings [here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSexGc2Z2Kp6bZW0D3_hfJ7NUUkfNHf7TXX-43FglCeBd9EF2Q/viewform?usp=send_form).

Next, we **share our work and offer feedback**. Depending on attendance, everyone gets \~10 minutes to use as they like. (No need to share, though; you’re welcome to come even if you prefer just to listen.)

We maintain a **Discord server** to help share our work and communicate outside our bi-weekly meet-ups. If you haven’t used Discord before, take a moment to download it and create an account before arriving. When we meet you on Saturday, we will add you to our server, the “DC Poetry Workshop”, and can help you navigate the app if you have questions.

Finally, if you plan on sharing a poem, consider how you will do so. Some options include:

* Print 5-10 copies to distribute in person
* Take and share screenshots in the Discord chat.
* Copy the poem into a google doc, change sharing settings to “anyone with link”, and copy the google doc link into the Discord chat.

Most importantly, we’re excited to meet you!

Catch you on Saturday,

Diego / Ian / Cayden / Nate / Otasha / Lia / An

📅 Our challenge runs from July through October

✨ **Description:** What if a walk in nature could nourish your well-being while helping others experience the healing power of the outdoors?
Join Imagine Well Being's Mindful Hiking Challenge and discover how simple acts of presence can create meaningful change- for yourself and for your community.
You'll explore beautiful landscapes, engage in mindfulness practices, and reconnect with the natural world in ways that inspire curiosity, gratitude, and wonder. Whether you hike a mountain trail, wander through a historic landscape, or pause beside a quiet stream, each step becomes an invitation to slow down, notice more deeply, and remember your connection to the living world around you.

To guide your journey, the challenge invites you to explore three distinct types of landscapes:

* **Historic Sites:** *Where we listen to the stories of the land.*
* **National Scenic Trails:** *Where the path guides us back to ourselves.*
* **National Parks:** *Where awe expands our perspective.*

⚙️ **How it Works**
You choose how, when, and where you explore. Complete the challenge at your own pace, and enrich your journey by joining our hosted, in-person community events—from hikes and bike rides to forest bathing, sound baths, and mindful movement.
📖 Participants receive a downloadable mindful hiking guide for each landscape, featuring sensory and creative invitations to explore with curiosity, deepen awareness, and discover what the land has to share.

💖 **The Impact:** A Practice of Reciprocity
Just like a healthy forest relies on an unseen network of roots to thrive, this challenge creates a beautiful cycle of mutual care between you and your community.

After his home is destroyed and his parents are killed in the Iran-Iraq war, Bashu, a small, dark-skinned boy from the Arabic-speaking Persian Gulf region of Iran, escapes on a truck to the northern part of the country, bordering the Caspian Sea. There he is taken in by Na’i, a peasant woman raising her own two children alone because her husband, who lost an arm in the war, is elsewhere in the country seeking employment. Since Na’i speaks only Gilaki, a local tongue, she and Bashu have no language in common. But over time they form a strong bond.

[Click here to watch a short scene from the film](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JSDcbZMVo58)

long_description:

Bring your own drum or use one of ours - no experience needed!

There will be loose guidance of a rhythmic drumming session, weaving in contemporary kirtan to inspire singing and dancing.

This is a donation-based gathering-pay what you can, with a suggested contribution of $15.

**🌿 About The Karma House**
The Karma House isn’t your average bar — we’re an alcohol-free kava bar and community hub in Lakewood, CO. Our space was created to bring people together through music, art, wellness, and connection. From live shows to poetry nights to wellness workshops, everything we do centers around community and creating a safe, welcoming atmosphere for all.
**🥥 What is a Kava Bar?**
Kava bars are unique gathering places where people come to connect and unwind without alcohol. Instead of cocktails, we serve traditional Polynesian kava — a calming root tea that has been used for centuries in the South Pacific for relaxation, stress relief, and social connection.
**🍵 What is Kava?**
Kava is made from the root of the Piper methysticum plant. It has gentle, grounding effects that can help calm the body and quiet the mind, making it perfect for relaxing, connecting, and enjoying good company. At The Karma House, we prepare our shells of kava with care and community in mind — it’s more than a drink, it’s a ritual of connection.

organizer: Firecraft Northwest Nature Bushcraft and Survival Outings
long_description:
During this hands-on workshop you’ll make your own basket from foraged Ponderosa Pine needles and a hand-made wooden base!
We’ll discuss how to identify the correct species for harvesting needles, when and how to harvest, and honorable and sustainable harvesting practices. Choose from multiple thread colors and wooden bases (unfinished, walnut oil finished or adorned with pressed flower) to add your own creative touch to your basket. Then, you’ll learn how to prepare your pine needles for basketry, practice multiple different stitches, understand and practice shaping walls, and learn about how to finish and seal your basket. We’ll finish the session with an overview of resources available to keep practicing on your own! Pine needle basketry is a slow and consistent craft, similar to knitting, crocheting, and embroidery - it requires a bit of patience and practice, but can be a very meditative and rewarding experience once you get the hang of it!
Please bring with you:

* A plastic bag or tupperware for transporting your basket home
* A plastic bag for taking home handfuls of soaked pine needles (gallon ziplock or larger)
* A hand towel
* Scissors
* Journal and pen for taking notes (optional)
* Mug/thermos for tea (optional)
* Water/snack (optional)
* Pliers (optional)
* Sit pad or camp chair for comfort (optional)

Register on Meetup or directly on our website to avoid a Meetup fee - https://www.firecraftnw.com/register/p/pine-needle-basketry-workshop-aug-2
